key_insight: Symmetry reshapes the Fourier spectrum of quantum Fourier models into orbit-wise symmetrized coefficients, giving a principled way to analyze and improve expressivity in geometric quantum machine learning.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical route to build invariant quantum models with better-controlled trainability, including an ancilla-free randomized encoding approach that avoids the extra depth of quantum twirling.
method: Organize Fourier coefficients into symmetry orbits and sum them into symmetrized coefficients.
Analyze variance under independent exact 2-design trainable layers, and derive bounds for ε-approximate 2-designs.
Use randomized encoding to implement invariant QFMs without ancillas or extra circuit depth.
evidence_signal: On two 2D QPINN benchmarks (screened Poisson and stationary viscous Hamilton-Jacobi), the hard-boundary models with exact symmetrization and randomized encoding achieved the lowest mean errors in their respective tests.
watch_item: The strongest guarantees depend on exact or near-2-design trainable layers, so performance and bounds may weaken if the ansatz deviates from these assumptions.
paper_title: Fourier Symmetrization for Geometric Quantum Machine Learning
